gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Thin steel rod, bent into shape, meets wide glass portholes. College is best at rod-like curves that never thin out, while Noto Sans Rejang is best at wide, open lowercase counters.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Authoritative from the first letter, College draws its arches with the weight of its stems. And Noto Sans Sharada, a sans-serif, brings bulky lowercase proportions and open c forms that never close up.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Approachable and wide-bodied, Noto Sans Siddham fills its line with a large central band. But College draws every stroke without any heavy-to-light shift, so the two meet as sturdy display and friendly text.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa is clean and modern, its open curves and lowercase filling most of the height. Let College go large, since its curves never thin at the turns.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: College draws every curve like spaghetti laid into letters, while Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes out before they touch. College earns its keep when it is big and brief.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri leaves every small round letter generously unclosed. Make College small and its curves, which never thin at the turns, lose the authority they have at size.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified, its terminals stopping far from the stem. Page after page, the text would feel open and generous, with College holding the top in unvarying strokes.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-tamil-su: Rope-like consistency runs through every stem, bowl and tail of College. And Noto Sans Tamil Supplement does its best work quietly, with round forms like open parentheses and a stocky middle band.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-telugu: College looks like wire of constant thickness bent into a sign. Noto Sans Telugu, a sans-serif with a high-set midline, gives that sign some plain text to sit beside.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-warang-c: Bent tubing turned into letters: that is College at a glance. Noto Sans Warang Citi, a plain sans, reads in solid blocks rather than skylines, with wide channels leading into each counter.
